tips.cue: Berries fully coloured and slightly soft.
tips.collect: Hand-pick whole berries.
tips.handling: Macerate and float off pulp. Most require both scarification and stratification, and are slow and unreliable from seed.

tips.cue: Calyces dry and brown, nutlets dark and hard inside.
tips.collect: Bend the stalk over a bag and tap - ripe nutlets fall out cleanly.
tips.handling: Winnow chaff gently; nutlets are small and blow away easily.

tips.cue: Pods leathery to papery and turning brown; seeds rattle loose inside.
tips.collect: Many pods dehisce explosively - bag whole infructescences before they twist open, or check plants every few days.
tips.handling: Hard-coated seed benefits from scarification before sowing. Freeze or heat-treat to kill bruchid beetle larvae, which are common.

tips.cue: Berries fully blue with a waxy bloom, and soft.
tips.collect: Clip whole umbels. Birds strip a plant in days once ripe.
tips.handling: Macerate and float off pulp the same day. Warm then cold stratify.

tips.cue: Coils uncurled and dry, nutlets hard.
tips.collect: Strip the uncurled coil into a bag.
tips.handling: Nutlets shed easily and are often lost to timing - check plants frequently.

tips.collect: Many pods dehisce explosively - bag whole infructescences before they twist open, or check plants every few days.
tips.handling: Hard-coated seed benefits from scarification before sowing. Freeze or heat-treat to kill bruchid beetle larvae, which are common.

tips.cue: Fruit fully coloured and slightly yielding.
tips.collect: Use tongs. Glochids are the real hazard, not the spines.
tips.handling: Macerate, rinse, dry thoroughly.

tips.collect: Many pods dehisce explosively - bag whole infructescences before they twist open, or check plants every few days.
tips.handling: Hard-coated seed benefits from scarification before sowing. Freeze or heat-treat to kill bruchid beetle larvae, which are common.

tips.cue: Berries fully coloured and soft.
tips.collect: Hand-pick.
tips.handling: Macerate, float off pulp, then cold-moist stratify.

tips.cue: Pappus (the fluff) has dried and begun to lift; heads look grey and open rather than green and tight.
tips.collect: Tug lightly - ripe achenes release with almost no resistance. If you have to pull, come back in a week.
tips.handling: Dries fast. Rub heads over a screen to separate achenes from chaff; many species have a high proportion of empty seed, so check fill by pinching.

tips.collect: Pick fleshy fruit by hand; strip plumed achenes when they detach at a touch.
tips.handling: Clean pulp from fleshy fruit promptly - fermenting flesh kills seed. Most need cold-moist stratification.

tips.cue: Berries turn green to red to black; collect at full black and soft.
tips.collect: Hand-pick - fruit ripens unevenly, so expect several visits.
tips.handling: Macerate, float, then cold stratify.

tips.cue: Schizocarp segments brown and separating from the central axis.
tips.collect: Roll the disc gently between fingers - ripe segments break away.
tips.handling: Hard seed coat; scarify before sowing.

tips.cue: Capsule has gone from green to straw and the seed inside is dark, not pale.
tips.collect: Capsules dehisce explosively. Bag them, or collect the moment the first few split.
tips.handling: Dry fully in a paper bag; seed threshes itself as remaining capsules open.

tips.cue: Drupes fully coloured and firm; on sumacs the sticky coating has developed.
tips.collect: Strip clusters by hand. Watch that fruit persists long after ripening - old grey fruit from last season is often still attached.
tips.handling: Remove the fleshy or waxy coat. Hard seed coat usually needs scarification.
tips.caution: Confirm identity - this family includes poison oak, whose fruit is also collected by birds and looks superficially similar at a distance.

tips.cue: Florets straw-coloured, seed firm; awns twist when dry.
tips.collect: Strip the seed head upward through a closed hand into a bag. Ripe seed shatters readily - a light shake tells you.
tips.handling: Keep well ventilated. Awned grasses tangle badly; leave awns on unless you are sowing with a drill.

tips.cue: Capsules darkening and the first few have already exploded.
tips.collect: Bag branch tips or lay a sheet - the window between ripe and gone can be under a week.
tips.handling: Dry in paper bags and let them self-thresh. Needs hot water followed by cold stratification.

tips.cue: Heads rust-coloured; rubbing releases hard, dark, three-angled achenes.
tips.collect: Rub heads between palms over a bag and check that real seed is coming out, not just chaff.
tips.handling: Screening is optional for direct sowing.
tips.caution: Dried flower heads persist for months after the seed has already dropped. A brown head is not evidence of seed.

tips.cue: Capsules splitting and cotton visible.
tips.collect: Collect the instant capsules open - viability is measured in days.
tips.handling: Sow immediately on wet mineral soil. Do not attempt to store.
